# Audio assets

Every non-code audio asset in Airline Empire: what it is, where it came from,
what it is for, and what a professional replacement should sound like.

Companion to `docs/AUDIO_ARCHITECTURE.md`, which covers the system that plays
them.

---

## 1. Provenance — read this first

**All 58 assets are original, generated by `scripts/audio/generate.py`.**

They are arithmetic: additive sine stacks, swept band-passed noise, and
hand-written envelopes, computed from scratch by a checked-in Python script
with no dependencies beyond the standard library. Nothing was sampled,
recorded, downloaded, purchased, or derived from any existing work.

| Question | Answer |
| --- | --- |
| Licence | None required. Original output of a script in this repository. |
| Third-party samples | **None.** |
| Sample libraries | **None.** |
| Recognisable commercial sounds | **None.** |
| Airline, film or game audio | **None.** |
| Reproducible | Yes — `python3 scripts/audio/generate.py` rewrites all 58 byte-identically (the noise source is a seeded LCG). |

### What these are not

**They are not the work of a sound designer, and nobody has heard them.**

This environment has no speaker and cannot run an iOS simulator. What is
verified is measurable: correct format, non-silent, click-free at both edges,
inside the mix ceiling, and following a deliberate loudness hierarchy. What is
*not* verified is whether any of it sounds good — see `docs/AUDIO_ARCHITECTURE.md`
§13 and task **AE-026**.

Treat them as a real, shippable first voice for the game and as **the brief for
their own replacement**. §4 below is written so that commissioning a
professional pass is a matter of handing that section over.

---

## 2. Format and conventions

| Property | Value | Why |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Container | WAV, PCM | Decoded once at launch into `AVAudioPCMBuffer`; no runtime decode cost, no codec dependency. |
| Channels | Mono | Every sound is a UI or notification event, none is positional. Stereo would double the size for nothing. |
| Rate | 44.1 kHz for cues, 22.05 kHz for music | Matches the engine's format, so no per-node sample-rate converter. |
| Depth | 16-bit | |
| Location | `AirlineEmpireApp/Resources/Audio/` | Flat. Not a folder reference — see `docs/AUDIO_ARCHITECTURE.md` §10 for the silent-failure this avoids. |
| Naming | `snake_case`, no extension in code | Named for the cue, never for the sound. |
| Total | 58 files, ~8.5 MB (54 cues + 4 music beds) | |

**Loop handling.** The two ambience beds are crossfaded onto themselves by
`loopable()` so the wrap is seamless; everything else is a one-shot that ends
in digital silence.

**Normalisation.** Each asset is normalised to a hand-chosen peak, not to a
uniform one — the peaks *are* the mix. An era change reaches 0.80; a tab tap
reaches 0.11. Category trims in `AudioEngine` are applied on top, baked into
the buffer at load.

**Ceilings, enforced by `scripts/audio/check-assets.py` in CI:** peak ≤ 0.85,
one-shots ≤ 3.5 s, every cue has exactly one file, every file has exactly one
cue, nothing effectively silent.

## 4. Production briefs

For a professional pass. Each brief is what the asset must *do*; the current
synthesised version is one answer to it, not the answer.

Rules that apply to every brief below:

- **Never**: casino coins, cartoon boings, cash registers, notification pings,
  camera shutters, riser-and-impact trailer clichés, anything with a
  recognisable instrument playing a melody.
- **Always**: an attack, however short. No sound starts at full amplitude.
- **Always**: end in silence. Overlaps are routine and must never click.
- **Tuning**: the palette sits on a D minor-pentatonic collection. Anything
  pitched should stay in it, so unrelated sounds still sound like one product.
- **Spectrum**: centred 200–2000 Hz with air above rather than sizzle. Nothing
  is bright merely to be noticed.

### Interface

**`ui_select`** · trigger: any selection change · purpose: the smallest
possible "yes, that registered" · 40–80 ms · peak 0.10–0.16 · attack ≤ 3 ms,
decay ≤ 40 ms · single soft partial around 800–1200 Hz · avoid: anything with
a discernible pitch *contour*; this fires hundreds of times a session and any
character becomes irritating.

**`ui_confirm`** · trigger: a committed action · purpose: closure, upward ·
150–250 ms · peak 0.30–0.36 · two elements a fifth apart, the second louder ·
avoid: fanfare. This is a full stop, not an exclamation mark.

**`ui_cancel`** · the same gesture falling · 120–200 ms · peak ≤ 0.28 · must be
recognisably the inverse of `ui_confirm`; the pair is the game's smallest
grammar and players learn it without being told.

**`ui_error`** · trigger: a refused command · purpose: "that is not available"
· 200–300 ms · peak ≤ 0.34 · low (150–250 Hz), two soft pulses, slightly
detuned · avoid: buzzers, harshness, anything that reads as scolding. The
player did nothing wrong; the game simply cannot do it.

**`ui_sheet_open` / `ui_sheet_close`** · purpose: a surface arriving/leaving ·
200–280 ms · peak ≤ 0.22 · filtered air moving up / down · avoid: whoosh
clichés; this must survive being heard fifty times an hour.

### Fleet

**`aircraft_delivered`** · trigger: an aircraft joins the fleet · purpose: an
object of real mass has arrived; second only to a route in importance ·
0.8–1.2 s · peak 0.60–0.68 · sub-weight (60–110 Hz) with a slow metallic bloom
above and a hint of air · avoid: an impact that reads as damage.

**`aircraft_ordered`** · a commitment made, delivery pending · 0.3–0.5 s ·
peak ≤ 0.38 · lighter than delivery, unresolved.

**`aircraft_assigned`** · a latch closing · 0.15–0.25 s · peak ≤ 0.42 · two
short bodies very close together · avoid: a click; this is mechanical, not
digital.

**`aircraft_sold`, `lease_returned`, `aircraft_unassigned`,
`maintenance_started`, `maintenance_completed`** · all ≤ 0.5 s, peak ≤ 0.35,
all deliberately unremarkable. These happen often and are not achievements.

### Routes — the signature

**`route_opened`** · trigger: a route opens · purpose: **the sound of the
game.** A line has been drawn between two cities and the network is now
larger. This is the one an audio director should get right first · 0.7–1.0 s ·
peak 0.55–0.62 · a rising three-note figure over a band of air travelling
upward, with low weight underneath · avoid: triumph. It should feel
*strategic* and *inevitable*, like a decision landing, not like a prize.

**`route_closed`** · the same figure descending · 0.5–0.7 s · peak ≤ 0.36 ·
avoid: sounding like failure. Closing a bad route is good management.

### Flights — the quietest family

**`flight_departed` / `flight_arrived`** · purpose: presence, not
announcement. These may fire many times a minute · 0.4–0.5 s · **peak ≤ 0.20**
· band-passed air travelling up / down, no pitch · avoid: engine recordings,
anything identifiable as a specific aircraft, anything a player could grow to
dread.

**`departure_flurry` / `arrival_flurry`** · trigger: several at once during
fast-forward · purpose: "the network is busy", once · 0.9–1.0 s · peak ≤ 0.26
· wider and *softer* than the individual it replaces · avoid: sounding like
several copies of the single event.

**`disruption_flurry`** · a bad morning, said once · ≤ 0.8 s · peak ≤ 0.38 ·
low, broad, unresolved.

**`flight_delayed` / `flight_cancelled`** · ≤ 0.4 s · peak ≤ 0.35 · a cancelled
flight gets low body; a delay is only a lean downward.

### The first times — the only sounds allowed to be beautiful

These four play at most once per campaign, so they can afford length and care
that nothing else can. They are the emotional spine of the first hour.

**`first_route`** · "my airline exists" · 1.5–1.8 s · peak 0.65–0.70 · the
`route_opened` figure, extended, with a fourth note and a longer air sweep.

**`first_departure`** · "my airline is *operating*" · 1.8–2.0 s · peak
0.70–0.75 · air building under something heavy, then release; a tonal swell
arriving in the second half · avoid: a literal take-off recording.

**`first_arrival`** · "it worked, and it came back" · 2.0–2.2 s · peak
0.70–0.78 · the same air travelling down, landing on a soft impact and
resolving upward · this is the payoff of the first twenty minutes.

**`first_revenue`** · "I built something that now pays" · 1.5–1.8 s · peak
0.68–0.72 · warm, major, the only unambiguously happy sound in the game ·
avoid: coins, registers, any money cliché whatsoever.

### Money

**`month_profit` / `month_loss`** · a statement closes · 0.6–0.7 s · peak ≤
0.44 · same shape, different colour: the profit resolves upward, the loss sits
down · avoid: making a loss sound like a failure state; most months are fine.

**`loan_taken`** · weight arriving with strings attached · ≤ 0.5 s · peak ≤
0.46 · low body, unresolved.

**`loan_repaid`** · ≤ 0.6 s · peak ≤ 0.40 · clean and quiet; relief, not
celebration.

**`solvency_warning`** · trigger: solvency crosses into `watch` · purpose: the
airline is being watched; there is still time · 0.4–0.6 s · peak ≤ 0.42 · two
low tones a semitone apart, the second lower · avoid: alarm. This must read as
a raised eyebrow, not a siren.

**`solvency_danger`** · trigger: the administration countdown starts ·
purpose: the last moment this game can be saved · 1.2–1.5 s · peak ≤ 0.60 ·
**the same interval as `solvency_warning`, lower, three times, slower**, over
a bed of low noise · the player must hear that this is the previous warning
getting worse rather than a new and different problem · avoid: startling
somebody into a panic decision.

### World — five distinct physical identities

**`world_storm`** · broad, moving, wet · 1.3–1.6 s · peak ≤ 0.46 · low
filtered noise with a descending sweep.

**`world_strike`** · mechanical, repeating, human · ~0.6 s · peak ≤ 0.42 ·
three even pulses · avoid: an alarm.

**`world_fuel_shock`** · a price moving the wrong way · ~1.1 s · peak ≤ 0.46 ·
one long unstable upward slide, slightly detuned against itself.

**`world_boom`** · the only good news in this family · ~1.1 s · peak ≤ 0.48 ·
open, bright, brief.

**`world_airport_closed`** · a door, not an alarm · ~0.6 s · peak ≤ 0.48 · low
body plus a closing filter sweep.

**`world_forecast` / `world_event_ended`** · ≤ 0.7 s · peak ≤ 0.26 · both
nearly subliminal.

### Progression

**`mission_completed`, `milestone`, `achievement`,
`capability_completed`** · 0.85–1.1 s · peak 0.48–0.52 · a shared family: the
player should hear that these four are the same *kind* of event · avoid:
game-show stings.

**`era_advanced`** · **the largest thing that happens to an airline** · the
only asset permitted past two seconds · 2.4–2.8 s · peak ≤ 0.82 · cinematic:
a low swell, a chord arriving late, a long air sweep, a high shimmer at the
end · this is the one place the game is allowed to be grand.

### The end

**`administration`** · trigger: entering administration · purpose: urgent by
*repetition*, never by volume · ~1.4 s · peak ≤ 0.62 · three low unresolved
pulses, slightly detuned · avoid: a jump-scare. The player is already in
trouble and does not need to be startled.

**`collapse` / `game_over`** · 2.2–3.0 s · peak ≤ 0.68 · long, low,
descending, no resolution · dignified. A failed airline deserves an ending,
not a raspberry.

### Ambience

**`ambience_operations`** (8.25 s loop) and **`ambience_world`** (10.25 s
loop) · peak ≤ 0.30, further attenuated to ~0.35 of the player's setting at
runtime · filtered air with a slow breathing swell and no identifiable events ·
**must survive an hour.** These are the weakest assets in the set and the
likeliest to need replacing: a convincing operations-room bed is a
field-recording problem, not a synthesis one.

## 5. Music

Four beds ship. They are **not a score**, and the distinction matters.

| Asset | State | Length | Rate | Peak |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `music_menu.wav` | No game in progress | 17.5 s loop | 22.05 kHz | 0.30 |
| `music_planning.wav` | A game, paused | 19.5 s loop | 22.05 kHz | 0.28 |
| `music_operating.wav` | A game, running | 21.5 s loop | 22.05 kHz | 0.30 |
| `music_crisis.wav` | Solvency in `danger` | 17.5 s loop | 22.05 kHz | 0.32 |

`MusicState.milestone` has **no track on purpose**: twelve seconds of different
music for a mission completion is a bigger interruption than the moment
deserves. The state exists so the bed can duck under the cue that marks it and
then return.

### What they are

Drones. Two or three sustained voices from the game's own pitch set, each
paired with a copy a few cents away so the two beat against each other on a
cycle of tens of seconds, low-passed hard, over a noise floor at 5%. There is
no melody, no rhythm, no chord change and no development of any kind.

That is a **deliberate ceiling, not a failed attempt at composition.** A pad
can be made tolerable for an hour by construction — there is nothing in it to
get stuck in your head, and nothing that arrives on a schedule you start
anticipating. A tune cannot: it either develops, in which case it competes
with the strategy, or it repeats, in which case an hour of route planning
becomes an hour of the same eight bars.

### Why 22.05 kHz

Nothing in a slow pad has content near 11 kHz, let alone 22. Half the rate is
inaudible here and halves the bundle: four beds at 44.1 kHz would have cost
3.4 MB, and cost 1.7 MB instead. They play through their own mixer node, which
converts, so the rate difference costs nothing at runtime.

### Constraints enforced in CI

`scripts/audio/check-assets.py` fails the build if a music bed exceeds **0.40
peak** (music must never be the loudest thing in the game), if its loop seam
is discontinuous by more than 0.02 (a click once per pass is the most
irritating defect an audio system can have), or if a state named by
`MusicDirector.asset(for:)` has no file — which would otherwise play a whole
game state silently.

### Brief for a composed replacement

If a composer replaces these, the four states are the deliverable, plus two
optional additions the state machine can already carry.

| Track | State | Length | Character |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `music_menu` | Main menu | 2–3 min loop | Still, wide, unhurried. The airline does not exist yet. |
| `music_planning` | Paused | 3–4 min | Sparse. Long notes, lots of space. The player is reading, comparing, deciding — this must not compete with thought. |
| `music_operating` | Running | 4–6 min | The default bed and the one heard for hours. **Must be genuinely ignorable.** |
| `music_crisis` | Solvency danger | 2–3 min | The same material, darker and thinner. A transition, not a new piece; it must not panic anyone into a bad decision. |
| *(optional)* `music_early` | Under ~5 routes | 3–4 min | Quietly optimistic, even sparser than planning. |
| *(optional)* `music_empire` | Late game | 4–6 min | The early theme, fuller. The reward for an hour of play is hearing where you started, grown. |

Requirements: original composition, full commercial rights, no recognisable
melody from any existing work; seamless loops; each ≤ 6 MB; peak ≤ 0.40. The
state machine, crossfades and settings are already built — adding a track is
dropping in a file with the right name.

---

## 6. Regenerating

```bash
python3 scripts/audio/generate.py      # rewrite all 58 assets
python3 scripts/audio/check-assets.py  # verify cues, files, format, ceilings
swift run ae-audio-manifest            # regenerate §3 of this document
```

Editing a sound means editing `scripts/audio/generate.py`. Do not hand-edit
the WAV files: they are build output, and the next regeneration would discard
the change.
